input:
Maya: hey all, i walked through the public kiosk route with the access checklist this morning. the trial build is on the lobby unit by the north entrance, not the staff demo one, so please use that hardware when you check anything. VoiceOver reads the opening screen, but i want one more pass with TalkBack because the speech order can differ. the main actions should announce as “Start a visit,” “Choose a language,” and “Get directions.” if you notice a label that sounds vague, can you drop the exact screen and wording here? i'm collecting the list before we freeze the test script, and we shouldn't assume that a visible button name is also what the screen reader announces.

Jonah: i checked the contrast pass on the lobby unit. the regular text on the cream panels is 7:1, and the large headings are 4.5:1, so both are above the targets we set for this trial. the selected-language state is the one place i’d like another look: the blue outline is a little thin when there's glare from the doors, even though the text itself passes. i can thicken the outline without changing the colors or moving the controls. Maya, can you confirm whether that fits the current build window? i haven’t changed it yet, and i’ll leave the existing version in place until we agree on the visual check for the selected state.

Priya: offline use is working for the visitor map and the building directory after the first load. i tested by turning off the lobby wifi, then reopening each page; the cached content was still there, and the kiosk didn't show a blank screen. the language menu also stayed available. one limitation to be clear about in the script: directions to the temporary gallery aren't in the offline package yet, since that room name comes from the live event feed. can we say that plainly before anyone starts the route? i don't want a visitor to think the whole kiosk is unavailable if that one listing can't load. the trial should still cover the main directory with wifi off.

Leo: quick audio update: play, pause, stop, and the speed setting are all reachable by touch, and they stay visible while the spoken directions run. the controls also have separate labels instead of just saying “button,” which helped during my VoiceOver pass. i set the default volume low because the lobby is quiet in the morning, but visitors can raise it with the on-screen slider. there’s no auto-play when a page opens. that should make it easier for someone to decide whether they want audio, and staff won't need to explain why the kiosk started speaking unexpectedly. i'll bring the headphones we use for the trial, but people can also listen through the built-in speaker.

Nora: for consent, the first audio prompt explains that speech is optional and asks before the kiosk records anything. To be clear, the trial build doesn't record speech or save names; the consent screen is there because the next version may offer a spoken question. a visitor can choose “Continue without audio” and reach the directory without accepting. i’d keep that option at the same size and prominence as “Allow audio,” rather than styling it as a small text link. please tell me if the current wording feels too technical when read aloud. i’ve drafted a shorter alternative, but haven't put it in the build because we should review it with the access group first.

Sam: i found one concrete bug on the lobby unit: after i change the language from English to Spanish, keyboard focus jumps to the browser chrome instead of staying on the language menu. Touch still works, but a keyboard user has to tab back into the kiosk. i can take this one and check both the language menu and the return path to the opening screen. it reproduces every time on the current build, so i’ll post here once i can verify a fix on the actual unit. i haven't seen it on the staff demo machine, which is why we should retest in the lobby. Please don't mark this as resolved based on the demo machine alone.

Inez: second bug from my pass: if i press Stop while the audio is playing, the speech stops but the screen reader still announces the audio control as active. the spoken directions don't restart unless i press Play again, so it seems to be a stale state label rather than the audio continuing in the background. i’ll own the check with Leo and compare the label after Stop, Pause, and Play. we should include a screen-reader check for that sequence in the script, not only a touch check. i can get the wording and the focus announcement back to everyone by Thursday at noon. Until then, let's leave the issue open and avoid telling staff the control state is fixed.

Omar: schedule proposal: we’ll run the public kiosk trial on Monday, October 14, from 10 a.m. to noon, with the access group and two volunteer visitors. I’ll meet everyone at the north entrance at 9:45 and bring the printed route cards; we can begin at 10 once the kiosk is reset. if anyone needs a quieter time for the audio check, we can use the small meeting room from 11 to 11:30, but the main trial stays at the lobby unit. Tuesday, October 15, from 1 to 3 p.m. is the backup slot only if the building closes the lobby on Monday. Please confirm by Thursday whether you can attend, and tell me if a volunteer needs a companion.

Tess: thanks, that gives us a clear plan. let's do the go/no-go review Friday, October 11, at 3 p.m. in this channel, after Sam and Inez post their checks and Nora confirms the consent wording review. the trial is a go only if both bugs are fixed and verified on the lobby unit, the screen-reader labels and audio states pass, and the access group has reviewed the consent screen. if any of those checks are still open at 3, the decision is no-go for Monday, and Omar can move the trial to the Tuesday backup slot after we confirm the lobby is available. please post evidence or a clear status for your item by then; a fix on the demo machine alone won't meet the check.

Maya: hey all, starting a thread for the three-day Harbor Week support rota, june 12-14. doors open at 8:30 am local each day, but the help desk starts taking tickets at 9. can we keep the rota in UTC too? the event page lists local times only and folks are joining from three regions.

Jon: yep. i'm in london, so that's BST, UTC+1. Priya's in New York on EDT, UTC-4, and Kenji's in Singapore, UTC+8. i'll put both columns in the sheet. please double check the midnight crossover for the last shift, because i don't want june 14 in one column and june 15 in the other by accident.

Maya: that split works for me, with one caveat: if an account lockout is stopping a speaker from getting into the venue, please page Dev too. that's not only billing at that point. i'll still own the customer reply, but Dev should decide whether the check-in system needs a workaround.

Kenji: yes, 11 pm to 3 am SGT friday night is the block i can do. on thursday it's 10 pm to 2 am. i'll add the date beside each one since the late shift crosses midnight, and i'll put the UTC times in a separate column rather than relying on the color key.

Anika: yes, and please keep the original language quote in the ticket if the customer wrote in German. the auto-translation sometimes turns room names into people's names, especially “Blue Hall.” i can review German wording, but i can't approve translations for Spanish or Japanese.

Jon: handoffs: whoever closes a shift should leave the ticket link, current status, last customer message time, and next action in the rota channel. no need to paste personal data into Slack. if the next person can't take it, they should say so in the thread rather than just adding a reaction and hoping someone sees it.

maya: quick q on undo in the drawing app — should undo remove only the last stroke? i was thinking about what happens when you reopen it, and i don't want reopening to clear the drawing.
dev: yeah, reopening shouldn't clear the drawing. that's separate from undo, though. undo should just take off the last stroke, not reset the whole canvas.
maya: right, i think i mixed those up in the ticket. i meant that if someone closes the app and comes back, their drawing is still there. undo shouldn't be doing anything on reopen.
sam: agreed on keeping those separate. cloud sync is its own issue too; let's not make this undo discussion depend on sync. the drawing should still be there after reopening, and undo should remove the most recent stroke.
maya: makes sense. the trade-off i'm wondering about is whether keeping undo that simple could surprise people who expect it to reverse more than one action, or is that enough for this change?
dev: not sure we need to decide the full undo history here. we can keep talking about the one-stroke behavior and leave the sync question separate.

Maya: Right, I think I mixed those up in the ticket. I meant that if someone closes the app and comes back, their drawing is still there. Undo shouldn't be doing anything on reopen.
Sam: Agreed on keeping those separate. Cloud sync is its own issue too; let's not make this undo discussion depend on sync. The drawing should still be there after reopening, and undo should remove the most recent stroke.
Maya: Makes sense. The trade-off I'm wondering about is whether keeping undo that simple could surprise people who expect it to reverse more than one action, or is that enough for this change?
Dev: Not sure we need to decide the full undo history here. We can keep talking about the one-stroke behavior and leave the sync question separate.

morning all, pulling the controller notes into one thread before we cut the next test pass. i tried the current dead zone values on the living room setup last night and the left stick still feels a little sleepy near center. at 0.18 it takes a noticeable nudge before the cursor moves, but dropping it to 0.12 made the hallway camera drift on my unit. can we keep the proposed 0.15 for now and log which pad we use when we compare? the numbers seemed different between the two controllers even with the same build. i'm not asking to lock a value yet, just want the next run to be comparable.

Dev — 9:18
yep, my xbox series pad on windows did the same thing at 0.18, but i didn't see drift at 0.15. i should say the test was in the old harbor scene, not the hallway, so that's not a clean comparison. can whoever has the elite 2 try the same scene and note whether the inner dead zone setting survives a restart? i changed the setting from the options screen, quit to desktop, reopened the game, and it was still 0.15. not sure if that confirms it saves for everyone or just my local profile. also the outer dead zone slider looked okay at 0.95, no obvious loss of full input on my pad.

Inez — 9:27
for remapping, i tested the dualsense on build pad-1842. face buttons and triggers can be swapped and the labels update in the pause menu, which is good. the issue i noticed is that remapping confirm to circle also makes circle back out of the keybind page, so i couldn't get back to the default layout without using the mouse. maybe i'm missing a separate back action. can someone with a switch pro controller check whether the same thing happens there? i didn't test that one yet. i'd rather not describe this as a bug until we know if there's a second binding for menu back somewhere.

Owen — 9:34
i have the switch pro here and got one reproducible menu issue on pad-1842. with focus on audio in the settings list, press right twice, then open the controller layout page and press b once. focus jumps to the first item in the left column instead of returning to the settings row. reopening settings and repeating those steps gives the same result. it doesn't happen if i enter the layout page from the title screen, only when i enter it from settings. i can record a short clip if useful. niko, could you own the focus check? i have the steps written down, but i don't know whether this is tied to the new focus navigation code or the remap screen.

Niko — 9:41
thanks, i can take the focus check. i'll use switch pro and xbox series pad, both wired, so bluetooth latency isn't another variable. i can check the title screen path and settings path on monday, may 20, then send the result before lunch. for the test matrix, please note windows 11 desktop, steam deck lcd, and steam deck oled as separate entries; the oled is on the beta client right now and the lcd isn't, so they aren't interchangeable. if anybody changes the build between checks, put the exact build label in the thread rather than just saying latest. i'll start with pad-1842 unless the next candidate is ready before then.

Rae — 10:03
captions check from me: dualsense on steam deck lcd, pad-1842, handheld mode. controller prompts update after i swap confirm and cancel, but the caption for the tutorial's long press still says press x even after i remap it to square. the general caption text is fine, only that button name stayed old in the prompt i saw near the ferry gate. i repeated the remap from a fresh profile and got the same text. i haven't checked the oled or the switch pro yet. can we keep this separate from the menu focus report? they might share a label source, but i haven't checked that and don't want to assume they do.

Sam — 10:16
second reproducible one is steam deck sleep and resume. on the oled with beta client, start a run in pad-1842, put the deck to sleep while the inventory wheel is open, wait about thirty seconds, wake it, then press the right stick. the inventory stays on screen and the game doesn't take the stick input until i press b, after which the normal pause menu appears. happened three times for me, each from the inventory wheel. with the lcd on stable client i got the wheel to close once on wake, but i haven't repeated that enough to call it a difference. i can own the resume repro and compare clients on tuesday, may 21.

Mara — 10:28
for dead zones, i put the xbox series pad and elite 2 side by side on windows 11, harbor scene, pad-1842. series pad at 0.15 looked centered, elite 2 drifted slowly left after about a minute at 0.15, and both stayed still at 0.18. i didn't touch the elite's accessory app between runs. that's only one elite sample, so please don't treat it as a general controller result. i can rerun with the same save on wednesday, may 22, and include 0.12, 0.15, and 0.18 in the notes. if someone can borrow another elite 2, that'd help tell us if this is the pad or the game setting.

Dev — 10:42
quote from the tester, keeping it exact: “I can tell the stick is centered, but the camera keeps taking tiny steps when I let go.” that was from the harbor scene on the elite 2, not the series pad. they were using the default camera speed and hadn't changed the accessibility sliders. i'm not sure whether those steps are the dead zone issue or the camera easing, so let's not connect them in the bug tracker yet. i can ask them to try the same input on the title screen too, but they'll need the test build installed again. does anyone still have the link to pad-1842 in the internal channel?

Inez — 10:55
i can send the link after this. also checked captions in the harbor scene on windows 11 with the xbox series pad, and the ordinary prompts reflect the remap after leaving and reopening settings. it's just the tutorial long-press line Rae saw that still has the old x label on deck. i haven't checked whether the caption appears after a scene reload or only the first time. i'll take that on pad-1842 tomorrow, may 20, with both the default layout and confirm-to-square. i don't want to mark captions clear based on the regular prompts, since the tutorial line is a different text entry.

Owen — 11:07
adding the retest plan so nobody has to piece it together from replies. these are checks, not fixes, and the owners can move the time if a build changes:
1. Niko: reproduce menu focus path on switch pro and xbox series, windows 11, pad-1842, monday may 20.
2. Inez: check tutorial long-press caption after scene reload with default and confirm-to-square, pad-1842, monday may 20.
3. Sam: compare steam deck oled beta client and lcd stable client for sleep/resume, pad-1842, tuesday may 21.
4. Mara: compare xbox series and a second elite 2 at 0.12, 0.15, and 0.18 in harbor, pad-1842, wednesday may 22.
please reply in this thread with the actual build label and steps you used, especially if you don't get the same behavior. if pad-1842 gets replaced before those dates, we should pause the comparison rather than mix results from different builds.

Mara — 11:15
one small request for everyone: when you report the controller, include wired or wireless, firmware if it is visible, and whether you changed anything in the device's own software. also say if the test was a fresh profile or an existing save; we had a couple of old options carry over during the last pass and it took a while to spot that. i don't need screenshots for every normal input, but a clip would help for the focus jump and deck resume if it's easy to grab. please don't reset a profile just to make a clip if you still need it for another test. i'll put the notes in the controller sheet once the retests come back, and keep the two reproducible reports separate for now.

input:
Mara — 9:02 AM
hey all, starting a thread for the May 16 community hour on Northside Community Radio. we're penciling in 6:00–7:00 pm, live from the studio, with a replay on Sunday. can everyone add what they need here? the running sheet is in the shared folder, but nothing is locked yet.

Jo — 9:07 AM
For guests, I have chef Amina Qureshi for the first half and garden organizer K'alia James for the second. Amina can come in person; K'alia said she may need to join remotely. I haven't sent the final confirmation to either of them, since we still need to check the segment lengths.

Mara — 9:12 AM
thanks. Jo, can you ask Amina how she says Qureshi? i heard two versions from different people and don't want to guess on air. and could we get K'alia to send a short voice note with her name too? I think it's pronounced kay-LEE-ah, but that's only my guess.

Jo — 9:18 AM
yep, I'll ask both. K'alia's last name is James, not Jaymes, per the email signature. I can send the voice note request today. For Amina, I'll ask if she wants a title used when we introduce her, rather than assuming chef is the wording she prefers.

Eli — 9:26 AM
Remote audio might be the tricky bit. We can send K'alia the browser link, but the studio laptop's mic is noisy and the spare USB interface is still with the youth program. If she has headphones and a quiet room, that should help. I can test the link with her before Friday, if she's available.

K'alia — 9:33 AM
I can do the link from home, probably from the back room. there's a fridge that clicks on every few minutes, though. I have wired earbuds with a mic, not a separate headset. Could someone tell me which browser you need? I'd rather not install anything the day of the show.

Eli — 9:41 AM
Chrome or Firefox should work, no install needed. the link is just in the browser. We should do a test call, but I don't know yet if Friday afternoon works for me; the school board meeting got moved and I'm helping with its recording. Could do Thursday after 4, or Saturday morning.

Mara — 9:48 AM
let's keep both test times as options until Eli checks. K'alia, would Thursday after 4 or Saturday morning suit you? We can also use the phone line as a backup, but I need to find out whether the board can feed it into the mixer without making the delay worse.

Noor — 10:03 AM
Music: I have three possible local tracks for the transitions, all under two minutes. The artists have said yes to being played at our outdoor events, but I haven't seen anything that covers radio or the online replay. I don't want to treat the event permission as broadcast permission, so I'll email them and ask specifically about both uses.

Noor — 10:11 AM
The files are “Rain on Cedar Street” by Lila Moss, “Market Morning” by Common Thread, and “Blue Tin Roof” by Sam Ortiz. We also need the station ident before the first track, unless the board wants the host to introduce the hour first. Does anyone know if the ident file we used last month is still the current one?

Jo — 10:18 AM
I can check the drive for the ident. For timing, my rough plan is a two-minute welcome, about twelve minutes with Amina, a short transition, then fifteen with K'alia. That leaves room for the calls, weather, sponsor mention, and music, but the whole hour is getting tight if either guest runs long.

Mara — 10:27 AM
yeah, and we haven't decided whether the call-in part is one block or two short ones. The draft has a break at 6:30, but that's where the garden segment would start. Maybe we can move the weather earlier, but Ben should say whether the forecast update is ready by then.

Ben — 10:34 AM
I can have the neighborhood forecast by 5:45. For weather backup, the city alert page is usually updated by 5:30, but it can lag if the radar warning comes in late. Should I prepare a short recorded forecast in case I can't get to the studio, or are we planning to read the city alert live?

Mara — 10:42 AM
please prepare the short recording, if you have time. We still need to decide who reads the city alert if it changes after your recording, and I don't want us to imply there's an active warning if there isn't one. Maybe keep the alert page open during the show and describe only what's posted at that time.

Tessa — 10:53 AM
I can handle captions for the replay, but I need the final running order and the guests' names before I make the cue sheet. The stream platform's auto-captions are available live, although they're often rough with names and street names. Is someone monitoring them during the broadcast, or is that still an open volunteer slot?

Luis — 11:02 AM
I have three volunteers who can help: Priya can run the front desk, Devon can watch the stream chat, and Max offered to do the time cards. None of them has confirmed the full hour yet. I'll check who's free on May 16 and whether anyone has experience correcting captions while the show is live.

Tessa — 11:10 AM
thanks. For my cue sheet, can you include the segment start times even if they're estimates? I can mark them as provisional. Also, if we do have someone watching live captions, they shouldn't be expected to edit the replay transcript too; that's a different chunk of work, and I can take the replay pass once the audio file is available.

Mara — 11:19 AM
Sponsor note: the draft says Harbor Bank, but their contact emailed a correction this morning. The wording they gave me is, “Our name is Harbor Credit Union, not Harbor Bank.” I'll fix the draft, but I haven't checked whether the sponsor mention is supposed to be before or after the first guest.

Jo — 11:26 AM
I'd put it after the welcome, before Amina, but we haven't promised them a position, right? I can check the agreement. Also, the draft sponsor line says they're supporting the whole hour; I'm not sure that's accurate, so let's not read that sentence until I find the signed copy.

Mara — 11:34 AM
right, no promise about placement that I know of. Jo, could you check the signed agreement and ask if the corrected name is enough, or if they want any other wording changed? The contact didn't mention a new line, just the name correction.

Devon — 11:47 AM
For calls, the draft says callers get 45 seconds and we have a seven-second delay, but I don't know if either part has been approved. Are we taking calls only about the garden project, or anything community-related? We should probably say what topics are welcome before we open the line.

Mara — 11:54 AM
the seven-second delay is what we used last month, not a decision for this show. The station manager needs to confirm that the delay box will be available. I also don't know if we want to limit calls to the garden segment; let's keep the policy unresolved until Jo checks with the manager.

Jo — 12:03 PM
I'll ask about the delay box, caller length, and topic policy together. We should also confirm whether callers give their names on air or can stay anonymous. I don't want to promise anonymity before we know how the call system records numbers, and I haven't found that information in the handbook yet.

Luis — 12:16 PM
Volunteer coverage is still a question too. If Devon is watching chat, someone else would need to manage the phone queue and tell Jo when the next caller is ready. Priya might be able to do it, but she said she's only sure about the front desk right now. I'll ask, not assign her.

Mara — 12:28 PM
great, thanks. For now the open items are name pronunciations, K'alia's audio test, music permissions, weather backup, exact timing, caption coverage, sponsor wording and placement, and the call-in rules. Please add updates in this thread rather than changing the running sheet yet, so we don't mistake a suggestion for a confirmed plan.

input:
maya: morning all, quick question about saturday's walk at the canal basin. i've got 8 people confirmed, maybe 2 more, and the footbridge is still closed for repairs. would you start at the north gate and do the east path out and back, or meet by the old pump house instead? the group includes two first-timers and one person using a cane, so i'm trying to avoid a route that looks fine on the map but gets muddy or narrow.

leo: i walked the east path yesterday around 9. the first 200 metres were dry, then there was a muddy patch beside the reed bed, maybe 10 metres long. it's passable in boots, but the gravel gets pretty uneven after the bench. i didn't see any signs saying the path was closed. there were three little egrets feeding near the drain, though they flew when a dog came through.

nina: fwiw the north gate has that new curb ramp now, but the latch on the pedestrian gate sticks. you have to pull it toward you pretty hard. i can get there early and hold it open if that's useful. the pump house entrance is wider, but the pavement on that side is cracked in two places and one of the cracks holds water after rain.

maya: thanks, this is exactly the sort of detail i needed. weather app says showers overnight friday, clearing by 8 saturday, but who knows. i don't want to promise a fully dry route. does anyone know whether the benches on the east stretch are still usable? last month one had a temporary barrier around it.

omar: i was there tuesday and the barrier is gone. the bench is fine, but the bin beside it is overflowing again. there was a pair of grey wagtails on the low wall, and i got a decent look from the path without stepping onto the wet grass. the construction crew had stacked boards near the second drain, not blocking anything when i passed.

jules: small heads up, the north gate is on Marlow Street, not the busier canal road. the 14 stops across from it every 20 mins on saturday morning, and there's a zebra crossing right by the gate. if we meet at the pump house, the nearest stop is another 6-minute walk and there's no crossing at the corner.

maya: good point about the bus. i'll put the meeting spot in the event post once we decide. i'm also thinking of splitting the walk into a shorter loop and an optional extra stretch, rather than asking everyone to keep pace together. nobody needs to bring binoculars; i have 4 loaners, plus two spare straps.

sanjay: for what it's worth, i took my dad along that route last weekend. he's steady on level ground but doesn't love loose gravel. he was okay as far as the bench, then waited there while i went another few minutes toward the willow. there are two places where the path narrows around shrubs, but people can pass if one person pauses.

bea: the willow stretch has been busy just after sunrise lately. saturday i counted 6 ring-necked parakeets in the plane trees and heard a great spotted woodpecker, but didn't see it. there was also a cyclist coming through fast near the narrow part. not trying to make it sound worse than it is, just worth mentioning if we have a few people walking together.

maya: appreciate the notes. to keep the plan clear, i'm leaning toward the north gate and an out-and-back to the bench, with the willow stretch as optional. if we do that, the round trip to the bench should be about 1.2 km, depending on where we stop to look. does anyone remember if there's a quiet place to do a quick bird count without blocking the path?

leo: there's a wider bit just past the bench, before the path bends toward the second drain. it fits maybe 5 people comfortably, not the whole group if everyone stands side by side. when i was there, a couple sat on the bench and the rest of us stayed back near the hedge. nobody seemed bothered, and we could still see the water from there.

nina: i'd suggest we gather at the gate, do introductions there, then walk in smaller pairs until the wider bit. otherwise we're all going to bunch up right at the entrance. i can bring a bright scarf so people can spot me if they arrive late. also, i have a folding stool, but i don't know whether it'll be useful on that gravel.

maya: that works. i'll add a note that late arrivals should wait by the north gate rather than try to catch up along the path. the group chat has a couple people who don't check the event page, so i'll send the same details here friday evening. should i include the bus number and the bit about the sticky latch, or is that too much detail?

omar: include both, maybe in a short access note. the bus detail is genuinely helpful, and the latch is the sort of thing that can make someone think they've got the wrong entrance. i'd say it sticks, but can be opened by pulling toward you. no need to mention the overflowing bin unless it gets worse by saturday.

jules: one more route detail: there are two low steps down to the water-viewing platform near the pump house. i didn't notice a ramp there, so that spot may not work for everyone. from the east path, you can see the same stretch of water from above, although reeds cover some of the near edge. i haven't checked whether the platform has changed since winter.

maya: thanks, i'll leave the platform off the main route. for the optional stretch, i can tell people we'll turn around before the narrow section if it's crowded or slippery. i don't want to imply everyone has to do it to count as joining the walk. could someone bring a paper map in case my phone signal drops by the basin?

bea: i can print the council path map tonight. it's the version dated march, and it shows the footbridge closure, but not the boards near the drain. i'll bring two copies and mark the north gate and bench with a pen. the map doesn't show the bus stops, so maybe add those separately in the message.

sanjay: i'll bring my small first-aid pouch and a couple of spare water bottles. not expecting anything, but it's useful to have on a group walk. i can also keep an eye on the back of the group if we split into pairs. just let me know whether we're still aiming to meet at 9:30, since the early bus gets in at 9:18.

maya: yes, let's keep 9:30 for now. i'll ask people to message if they're running late rather than waiting for the whole group, but nobody should feel rushed. i can arrive at 9:15 to check the gate and see how wet the path is. if the muddy patch looks worse than described, we can decide there whether to stop at the bench or turn back sooner.

leo: sounds sensible. i'll bring binoculars and the little bird checklist from last month's walk. it has the common canal species on one page, which is easier than passing around a phone. i'll add any sightings after we finish, but i won't try to keep a count while we're walking unless someone else wants to do that.

maya: one last thing before i update the event: should the description say that the route is about 1.2 km to the bench and back, with an optional extra stretch, and that the east path may be muddy after rain? i'll include that there are no toilets along the path, and that the nearest public toilets are at the library on Marlow Street. please flag anything i've missed.

input:
Mara: quick saturday update from the eastbank birding walk. we had 11 people at the boathouse at 7:10, and the path was dry except for the stretch by the willow gate. cloud cover kept the light soft for most of the morning

Dev: i got there a little after seven, so i missed the first check in. the river was high from thursday's rain, but it hadn't reached the lower bench. there was a lot of mud around the map board

Lina: the first bird we logged was a song sparrow near the bike rack. it kept singing from the same low branch while people were arriving, then flew into the reeds when a jogger passed

Owen: i counted three great blue herons along the far bank, not all at once. one was near the footbridge, and the other two were farther south by the old stone wall. hard to tell if they were the same birds moving around

Mara: we also heard a barred owl from the cemetery side at about 7:35. nobody saw it, and the call was brief, maybe two rounds. that area is outside the park boundary but still audible from the path

Priya: thanks for noting that. i had the Merlin app open and got a match for barred owl, but i wouldn't count that as a visual sighting. the app was slow to load with the weak signal near the river

Cal: the kingfisher was back at the footbridge, or at least one was there. it perched on the railing for maybe a minute, then went downstream. i saw it dive once but didn't see whether it caught anything

Dev: quick note on access: the north gate was unlocked when i arrived, and the small gravel lot had room for four cars. the water fountain by the playground is still covered, so bring bottles if you're coming next week

Lina: i found two mallards with ducklings in the inlet beside the community garden. i counted five ducklings, though they kept vanishing behind the grass. please give that corner plenty of space if you walk through

Owen: there were also cedar waxwings in the crabapple trees on Mercer Street. i saw a flock of around 14, but they moved before anyone else got a clear count. one of them had a berry and dropped it on the sidewalk

Mara: for the shared log, i have these as the main notes
1. song sparrow at the east bike rack, singing at 7:12
2. barred owl heard from cemetery side, not seen
3. kingfisher at the footbridge railing, then downstream
if i missed something important, add it here before tonight

Cal: i noticed a red-tailed hawk circling above the water tower around 8:05. it was high up and only stayed in view for a few seconds, so i didn't get a good look at the tail. could've been a hawk, but red-tail is my best guess

Priya: that sounds fair. i saw a hawk over the school field last month, but i can't say it was the same one. the field wasn't part of saturday's route, and i didn't log anything from there this time

Dev: on the walk back, the maintenance crew had put a cone near the cracked paving stone by the south steps. the stone is still uneven, so watch your footing there. nobody from our group used the ramp by the boathouse

Lina: the community garden volunteers were watering beds when we passed at 8:20. one of them asked whether we were looking for the nesting box near the shed. we said we were checking the riverside trail, not the garden boxes

Eli: i spoke with Jo from the garden group after everyone left. Jo said the box had been checked on friday and there wasn't a nest in it. i didn't ask what species they usually get there

Mara: small correction to my first note, we had 12 people total, not 11. Ben joined by the bridge and didn't make it to the boathouse check in. sorry, i noticed his name missing when i looked at the sign-up sheet

Owen: no worries, and thanks for fixing it. the group stayed together until the garden inlet, then split into two pairs for the last stretch. we met back at the south steps just before nine

Priya: for next saturday, forecast says light rain before sunrise and cloudy after eight. that's just the forecast as of this morning, so check again before heading out. the route is still listed as the river loop on the calendar

Cal: i can bring the spare binoculars next week. the left eyecup is loose, though, so i'll put a note on the case. they're fine to use if you keep the cup from turning while you focus

Lina: i'll bring the printed map with the garden boundary marked. a couple people asked where the park ends by Mercer Street, and the online map labels that path differently from the sign at the south steps

Dev: does anyone have the exact time we passed the herons? i wrote 7:50 in my notebook, but that was after we crossed the footbridge and may be a few minutes late. i don't want to make it sound more exact than it was

output:
Mara: Quick Saturday update from the Eastbank birding walk. We had 11 people at the boathouse at 7:10, and the path was dry except for the stretch by the willow gate. Cloud cover kept the light soft for most of the morning.

Dev: I got there a little after seven, so I missed the first check-in. The river was high from Thursday's rain, but it hadn't reached the lower bench. There was a lot of mud around the map board.

Lina: The first bird we logged was a song sparrow near the bike rack. It kept singing from the same low branch while people were arriving, then flew into the reeds when a jogger passed.

Owen: I counted three great blue herons along the far bank, not all at once. One was near the footbridge, and the other two were farther south by the old stone wall. Hard to tell if they were the same birds moving around.

Mara: We also heard a barred owl from the cemetery side at about 7:35. Nobody saw it, and the call was brief, maybe two rounds. That area is outside the park boundary but still audible from the path.

Priya: Thanks for noting that. I had the Merlin app open and got a match for barred owl, but I wouldn't count that as a visual sighting. The app was slow to load with the weak signal near the river.

Cal: The kingfisher was back at the footbridge, or at least one was there. It perched on the railing for maybe a minute, then went downstream. I saw it dive once but didn't see whether it caught anything.

Dev: Quick note on access: The north gate was unlocked when I arrived, and the small gravel lot had room for four cars. The water fountain by the playground is still covered, so bring bottles if you're coming next week.

Lina: I found two mallards with ducklings in the inlet beside the community garden. I counted five ducklings, though they kept vanishing behind the grass. Please give that corner plenty of space if you walk through.

Owen: There were also cedar waxwings in the crabapple trees on Mercer Street. I saw a flock of around 14, but they moved before anyone else got a clear count. One of them had a berry and dropped it on the sidewalk.

Mara: For the shared log, I have these as the main notes:
1. Song sparrow at the east bike rack, singing at 7:12.
2. Barred owl heard from the cemetery side, not seen.
3. Kingfisher at the footbridge railing, then downstream.
If I missed something important, add it here before tonight.

Cal: I noticed a red-tailed hawk circling above the water tower around 8:05. It was high up and only stayed in view for a few seconds, so I didn't get a good look at the tail. Could've been a hawk, but red-tail is my best guess.

Priya: That sounds fair. I saw a hawk over the school field last month, but I can't say it was the same one. The field wasn't part of Saturday's route, and I didn't log anything from there this time.

Dev: On the walk back, the maintenance crew had put a cone near the cracked paving stone by the south steps. The stone is still uneven, so watch your footing there. Nobody from our group used the ramp by the boathouse.

Lina: The community garden volunteers were watering beds when we passed at 8:20. One of them asked whether we were looking for the nesting box near the shed. We said we were checking the riverside trail, not the garden boxes.

Eli: I spoke with Jo from the garden group after everyone left. Jo said the box had been checked on Friday and there wasn't a nest in it. I didn't ask what species they usually get there.

Mara: Small correction to my first note: We had 12 people total, not 11. Ben joined by the bridge and didn't make it to the boathouse check-in. Sorry, I noticed his name missing when I looked at the sign-up sheet.

Owen: No worries, and thanks for fixing it. The group stayed together until the garden inlet, then split into two pairs for the last stretch. We met back at the south steps just before nine.

Priya: For next Saturday, the forecast says light rain before sunrise and cloudy after eight. That's just the forecast as of this morning, so check again before heading out. The route is still listed as the river loop on the calendar.

Cal: I can bring the spare binoculars next week. The left eyecup is loose, though, so I'll put a note on the case. They're fine to use if you keep the cup from turning while you focus.

Lina: I'll bring the printed map with the garden boundary marked. A couple of people asked where the park ends by Mercer Street, and the online map labels that path differently from the sign at the south steps.

Mara: I'll put approximately 7:45 to 7:55 in the log. Thanks, everyone, for the notes and for keeping space around the ducklings. I'll post the final list after I check the times against the photos.

Dev: Yeah, I checked it too. Jules booked a rear-wheel tune-up and a brake check on Tuesday, then brought the bike in Thursday morning. We found a cracked rim near the valve, so the original wheel couldn’t safely stay in service. The replacement rim was a different price from the basic truing estimate, and I should have called before starting that extra work.

Lena: The review says, “Everyone was kind, and the bike feels great, but I didn’t know the total until pickup.” That’s fair. The front desk did mention that we’d inspect the wheel, but I don’t see a note that anyone explained the possible parts cost or got Jules’s go-ahead. We can acknowledge that gap without making it sound like the repair itself was in question.

Owen: For context, the rim arrived from Northline on Friday at 10:20, and Dev finished the build just before lunch. Jules collected the bike at 4:15. The invoice shows the rim, new spokes, and labor as separate lines, but I agree that seeing those line items only at checkout isn’t the same as hearing the revised estimate beforehand. Let’s keep the reply plain and human.

What missed: the price changed after we found the cracked rim, and we didn’t clearly explain the new total before proceeding. 3. What to say back: apologize for the surprise, thank Jules for pointing it out, and invite them to contact us if they want to talk through the invoice. Does that sound right?

Inez: Yes, and I’d avoid saying “we always call” because that’s not what happened here. The intake card has a $180 approval limit, but the replacement wheel work came to $246. We should say we should have paused and checked with Jules once the repair was going beyond the initial estimate. That owns the specific issue without promising a policy change we haven’t discussed.

Dev: Agreed. I remember the conversation at the bench, but I talked about the rim being cracked and didn’t give a number. I thought the service writer had already covered it; the work order shows that neither of us recorded a revised quote. Jules shouldn’t have had to ask at pickup why the bill was higher. I’m happy to be named in the reply if that feels appropriate, though it doesn’t need a staff name.

Priya: Maybe keep the answer in the shop’s voice, rather than making it about one person. Something like, “Thanks for taking the time to leave this feedback. We’re glad the bike is riding well, and we’re sorry the updated cost came as a surprise at pickup. After finding the cracked rim, we should have explained the revised estimate and checked with you before moving ahead.” That’s clear and doesn’t dodge it.

Owen: I like that. Could we mention the original estimate was for truing and a brake check, but not list every part? The public reply doesn’t need the whole invoice, and a detailed breakdown might read as if we’re arguing with the review. If Jules asks us directly, we can explain the rim and spoke costs in a private conversation. We have the old rim set aside until next Wednesday.

Lena: Good point. I’d add a warm closing, but not “we hope you’ll give us another chance,” since that can put pressure on someone who just gave useful feedback. Maybe thank them again and say they’re welcome to get in touch with Mara at the shop if they have questions about the invoice. We should use the email address listed on the receipt, not ask them to post personal details publicly.

Mara: That works. The response can be short even though we’ve got a lot of context here. I’ll check the receipt for the right contact details before posting. Also, let’s not mention the Friday delivery delay; it didn’t change the price issue, and Jules didn’t raise timing as a concern. The bike was ready the same day the rim arrived, and that’s useful for our internal notes, not necessarily the public reply.

Inez: One small detail: the review calls it a “rear wheel tune-up,” while our booking calendar says “rear wheel true + brake check.” We don’t need to correct Jules’s wording. The useful point is that the initial estimate covered the requested inspection and adjustment, then the cracked rim meant extra parts and labor. I’m glad we looked at the actual work order instead of guessing from memory.

Dev: Same here. I’ll add a reminder to the morning handoff notes: if inspection finds damage that changes the quoted total, stop and contact the customer before continuing. That’s just a reminder for our current process, not a new rule from this thread. We can also check that the approval-limit field is visible on the tablet; it’s easy to miss below the parts notes.

Priya: Thanks, everyone. The draft feels fair to Jules and to the people who did the repair. I’ll send it to Mara for a final look before it goes up, and we can keep the invoice details handy in case Jules follows up privately. Appreciate the thoughtful read, especially the point about not turning a sincere apology into an explanation of why the shop was busy. 🚲

hey folks quick baking update, i made the cinnamon rolls again this morning and tried the smaller pan we talked about. the dough was easier to handle after chilling it for 30 minutes, and i used oat milk because thats what i had open. they needed about 4 minutes longer than the recipe said, probably because the rolls were packed pretty close together. the centers came out soft, though, and the edges browned more evenly than last time.

output:
Hey folks, quick baking update: I made the cinnamon rolls again this morning and tried the smaller pan we talked about. The dough was easier to handle after chilling it for 30 minutes, and I used oat milk because that's what I had open. They needed about 4 minutes longer than the recipe said, probably because the rolls were packed pretty close together. The centers came out soft, though, and the edges browned more evenly than last time.

I also mixed the icing while they cooled, but it was a little runny at first. I added another couple spoonfuls of powdered sugar, and that fixed the texture. There are six left in the blue container on the counter if anyone wants one later. I wrote the extra bake time on the recipe card, but didn't change the ingredient amounts. Next time, I'll try putting the pan on the middle rack from the start; today it was on the lower rack for the first 10 minutes because the oven was still warming up. Overall, pretty happy with how this batch turned out 🙂

Priya: yep, I can bring the bag. I’m picking up Nori’s blanket from the laundromat at 4, so library by 4:20 is probably easiest. Nori’s going to stay with Ben on Saturday, right? Her foster form says she gets worried around scooters, and the path outside the laundromat is always busy with kids on them.

Ben: right, Nori’s staying with me. I can meet Priya at the side entrance, not the main doors, because Nori pulls toward the bakery next door and there’s usually a line. I’ve got the green harness from her last visit, but can someone check that it still fits? She’s gained a little weight since then, maybe a pound or so.

Tess: I can check the harness Friday evening when I bring over her meds. The label says one tablet with dinner, and I’ll put the bottle in a zip pouch with the printed instructions. She finished the antibiotics last week, so those aren’t part of the Saturday bag. I’m not sure if the appetite note in her folder is up to date, though.

Maya: good catch. The appetite note is from Tuesday, when she skipped breakfast but ate dinner. We haven’t heard that she’s done it again. Ben, could you just message the group if she skips a meal this weekend? No need to change the tablet schedule unless the clinic tells us to.

Leo: for the other two, I can take Otis from the west-side pickup point at 11 on Saturday, then drop him with Sal around noon. Sal, does that still work? His transport sheet says he gets carsick if he eats right before the ride, but I don’t know whether that means no breakfast or just no snack before we leave.

Sal: noon works. I can keep Otis through Sunday night, and I’ve got the washable bed he used here in January. Last time, he ate breakfast at 7 and didn’t throw up in the car, so maybe that timing is fine. I’ll bring paper towels anyway. The west-side point is the pharmacy lot, yes, not the church lot?

Leo: pharmacy lot, yep. I’ll send a pin Saturday morning, since the map app sometimes puts people behind the building. Otis’s carrier is in my trunk, but the latch sticks if you close it too fast. I’ll show you how it works before we leave, and I can bring his blanket too.

Rhea: one more thing on Pippin, his foster notes say he barks when someone knocks, but he settled after a few minutes here. I can put a note on my door asking visitors to text instead. Is there anything specific I should do if he keeps barking, or should I just give him space and let him settle? I don’t want to make it worse by trying a training trick I haven’t been shown.

Maya: giving him space is fine for now, and please don’t try a new training approach without checking with the behavior team. If he seems panicked or you notice anything unusual, call the on-call number in the folder. It’s staffed until 9 p.m.; after that, send a text and they’ll reply when they can. We don’t know yet whether the behavior team can visit this weekend.

Priya: i found the weekend sheet and there’s a little mismatch on Otis’s dropoff time. One page says Sal at noon, the other says 12:30. Sal, if noon still works, I’ll mark the second sheet too. Also the supply closet code changed to 4816 last week, in case anyone has the old one saved.

Sal: noon is still good. I’ll text Leo when I’m leaving home, because the pharmacy lot gets backed up if there’s a delivery truck. I can wait ten minutes, but after that I have to head back for a work call at 12:45. If the pickup runs late, please let me know before I leave.

Maya: thanks, all. My actual question is whether we should make one shared handoff window at the library for Pippin and Nori, or keep those as separate meetups, given Priya’s 4:20 timing and Ben’s side entrance plan. I can update the weekend sheet tonight, but I’d rather not put everyone in one crowded spot if that’ll make Nori’s scooter stress harder to manage.

mina: hey all, north quay film collective emailed about filming a short scene in the lower gallery on saturday, may 18. they asked if they can bring six people, two cameras and a small battery light, and move the replica fishing net for a cleaner shot. they'd like the room for about three hours, before we open if possible. they said the scene is set in the 1930s and the museum would be credited.

jules: thanks, mina. did they say whether the cameras are handheld, and if they'll need to put anything on the walls or floor? the lower gallery has the painted harbor panel and the case with the bronze hooks, so even a small setup might need more space than it sounds like. also, is their date fixed, or could we offer another day?

mina: i asked. handheld cameras, no wall mounts, and they can use the west entrance for their cases. saturday is the only day all six people are available. they were hoping to film from 8 to 11, then have a few still photos by the old map. they asked whether we could keep the doors closed until they're done.

ravi: i'm afraid we can't let a production use the lower gallery that morning. the gallery is scheduled for the school group's object-handling session at 9:30, and we can't move that booking. the painted harbor panel also has a light limit; a battery light still counts as additional exposure, even if it's only on briefly. i'd rather be clear about that now.

mina: agreed. i can send a polite no for the gallery and the 8 to 11 slot. could we suggest the education room instead? it has plain walls, a table they could dress as a workbench, and no original objects on display. i don't know if that gives them the old harbor look they want, though, or if they'd need a later date.

jules: the education room is free on saturday until noon, according to the shared calendar. the large harbor photograph is stored in the rolling cabinet, but it's not for filming or display without approval from collections. we can offer the room without promising that image. there's also the covered courtyard, although rain would make that a poor backup for cameras.

mina: for the reply, maybe list the options so they can decide what works. 1) we can't provide the lower gallery on may 18, because of the school booking and the panel's light limit. 2) we can ask whether the education room, 8 to 11, would suit them. 3) we could check a weekday in june for gallery availability, but no date is held yet.

ravi: that reads well. please don't say the weekday is available until we check the school calendar and collections rota. the first week of june has two visiting classes on tuesday and thursday, and our conservator is doing a condition check in the lower gallery on wednesday. friday the 7th looks less crowded in the calendar, but it's still only a possibility.

mina: yep, i'll keep it as a possible date to check, not an offer. the collective also asked whether the replica fishing net can be moved into the education room. it's on a labeled stand in the gallery and isn't fragile, but the stand is awkward through the corridor. does anyone know if it can be moved safely, or should i leave that out for now?

jules: i'd leave it out until collections checks the stand and route. the net was made for the 2018 harbor exhibit, and one of the wooden supports has a loose joint. it might be fine to move with two people, but we shouldn't promise that before someone has looked at it. we can mention that we may be able to discuss a replica prop later.

ravi: one more detail: they asked if they could use the museum logo on the end card. we can say the film credit is welcome, but use of the logo needs a separate request to communications. that isn't a yes yet. if they're interested in the education room, ask them to send a short description of the scene and their equipment list first.

mina: got it. i'll thank them for thinking of the museum, explain that we can't host filming in the lower gallery on may 18, and offer to check the education room for 8 to 11. i'll also say we can look at a weekday in june, without holding friday the 7th, and that the net and logo would need separate checks.

jules: sounds good. for the room, facilities should confirm access and the table setup before we describe it as ready. there are two folding tables in storage, but one has a wobbly leg and the other is usually used by the oral history team. we can say the room may be an alternative, not that every prop or setup is included.

ravi: and let's be clear that we'd need them to wrap before noon if that room works, because the family archaeology workshop starts at 12:30 and staff need time to reset. no need to get into every detail in the first email, but a simple note about the time limit is useful. we shouldn't imply the workshop can move.

mina: i'll send the draft to you both before it goes out. it'll decline the gallery request, offer the education room as an alternative subject to checking, and invite them to share the scene description and equipment list if they'd like us to explore it. no date or object use is confirmed yet.

input:
Maya: morning all, sharing the visitor feedback from the weekend before we lock the archaeology gallery labels. One person wrote, “the room is beautiful, but I couldn't tell which objects came from the same site.” That's fair, and I think we can answer it without making the cases feel crowded.

Jon: thanks for pulling that together. The current map has the site names in tiny gray type, and the labels put dates first. Visitors are probably looking for a simple link between the pottery, tools, and the place they came from.

Maya: exactly. I can move the site name to the first line and add a small map key beside the entrance panel. I don't want to promise that every object has a confirmed findspot, though. Some came through older collections with incomplete records.

Ravi: good point. The blue bowl from Tell Aran has a documented excavation record, but the two copper pins only say “northern valley” in the 1938 ledger. Could the map show the broad region for those, rather than a precise dot?

Maya: yes, that's safer. I checked with collections this morning, and they said “northern valley” is all we can support for the pins. The bowl can have a site marker, with a note that it was found in a domestic courtyard.

Leah: I like that distinction. One other bit of feedback said the labels were hard to read from a wheelchair. The lower case is fine, but the text near the carved stone is partly behind the bench when someone parks there.

Jon: I measured it yesterday. The bench is 14 inches from the case, so a seated visitor can see the first paragraph, but not the last two lines. We could shift the bench left about a foot without blocking the doorway.

Leah: let's test that before we move it for good. Facilities can mark the floor today, and we can ask the access group to check the sightline on Thursday. Please keep the bench move as a trial, not a confirmed change.

Maya: noted. For the labels, I suggest this order:
1. site and region
2. object name and date
3. one short sentence about how it was used

That should answer the feedback and still leave space for the image credit. We shouldn't add a paragraph explaining the whole excavation history to every case.

Ravi: agreed on keeping it short. The stone scraper label already says “probably used to prepare animal hides,” which is appropriately cautious. Can we keep “probably” there? The use is based on wear marks, not a direct record.

Maya: absolutely, we shouldn't turn that into a definite claim. I'll leave the wording as it is. For the new map key, I can use solid circles for documented sites and a shaded band for broad regional records.

Jon: that seems clear. Can we also add a small note under the key explaining that the shaded area isn't a precise findspot? Otherwise people might assume we know the exact village. There is room below the scale bar, I think.

Ravi: yes, and let's keep the map itself at the entrance. The visitor comment mentioned wanting to connect objects across cases, so a single key there might help more than repeating a mini map on every label.

Leah: small concern: the entrance panel is already busy, with the gallery title, the loan acknowledgement, and the route arrow. Maybe we can remove the decorative compass rose? It looks nice, but it doesn't explain anything about the collection.

Maya: I can ask design to mock that up, but I don't want to remove it before we see the map at actual size. The panel is 32 inches wide, and the compass rose is about 5 inches across.

Jon: fair. Let's get two proofs, one with the rose and one without, and check both from the doorway. Also, the loan acknowledgement has to stay exactly as approved by the lender; please don't shorten that line to make the map fit.

Maya: yep, I'll flag that for design. The label printer can do the larger site name in the same typeface, but increasing it may add a line on the two longest labels. I can bring a proof to the review rather than guess.

Ravi: while you're doing that, could we check the dates on the three objects from the west trench? The draft says 600–500 BCE for all three, but the catalog has 550–450 BCE for the bronze awl. I may be reading an old record.

Maya: I'll ask collections to verify the awl today. Until they confirm, let's not change the date or print the label. The pottery and spindle whorl are listed as 600–500 BCE in the current catalog.

Leah: thanks. For Thursday's access check, I'll bring the large-print draft and the floor plan. Can someone also check glare around 2 p.m.? The west window makes the glass case bright then, and that might affect the label readability too.

Jon: I can be there at two. I'll bring the portable light meter, though we don't need to treat one reading as a final assessment. The blinds were adjusted last month, so let's note their position as well.

Maya: great, thanks. I'll reply to the visitor through the feedback form once we have the label proofs and the sightline notes. For now I can say we're reviewing the map and readability, not that we've made the changes.

Ravi: good. Could we keep the feedbacker's wording anonymous in the design notes? No name was included, but the form has a visit date and party size. We only need the actual comment for this discussion.

Maya: yes, I'll share just the comment, with the date and party details removed. I'll post the proofs here when design sends them, likely Wednesday afternoon. If the awl date isn't confirmed by then, I'll mark that line for review.

Leah: sounds good. I'll reserve Thursday at 10:30 with the access group, and Jon can join at two for the glare check. If either time changes, please update this thread so we don't assume the checks happened.

Jon: done. I'll ask facilities to put down removable tape for the bench trial, not move the bench yet. That gives us a clear position to test and keeps the doorway route open. 🙂

Maya: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll collect the open items in the review note and keep the feedback reply pending until we have something concrete to report.

Dev: I walked the shoreline at lunch. There are fishing lines wrapped around the driftwood near the old lifeguard stand, plus a cracked cooler partly buried in the sand. I didn’t touch either one. Can someone bring work gloves and a sturdy pair of cutters?

Nia: I can bring gloves, cutters, and the orange buckets from the storage shed. The shed key is with me. I’m not sure whether the little blue cart still has a working wheel, though, so we may need to carry supplies by hand.

Luis: I can bring my hatchback, but I can’t take loose glass or anything leaking in the car. Is anyone able to bring a lined tote for the glass? I’ve got two thick contractor bags for ordinary litter and wet rope.

1. Bring a first-aid kit and extra water.

3. Keep the path to the gate clear while bags are collected.

Mara: I can bring two medium pairs from home. Also, if anyone has a folding table, could you bring it for the sign-in sheet and supplies? We can manage without one, but it’d be useful if the ground is damp.

Luis: I’ll bring my small folding table and keep it by the boardwalk entrance, not the pickup area. Please reply here if you can help carry bags uphill or if you have questions about what should be left for the ranger.

input:
mara: quick question before thursday’s work party: can we test the south-bed water line at 9:30, or is that too early for the pump? we’ve got new timers to install, and i don’t want to tell folks to bring tools if the water will be off.

jon: 9:30 should be ok, i think. the pump is on the same circuit as the shed lights, but the timer for it is separate. last week it started around 10, though i wasn’t here when someone changed the setting. i can check the panel tonight.

priya: adding context: we have 28 plots on that line, and the two new beds by the fence are using the temporary hose. if we test with every tap open, the pressure drops a lot. maybe start with just the south row and see what the gauge says?

owen: that sounds sensible. the gauge is in the little green box by the tool shed, not the one near the compost bays. the glass has a crack but the needle still moves. i’ll bring the spare gauge from my garage just in case.

mara: thanks. the work party note currently says “water check at 9,” so i can update that once we know. also, the north gate sticks when it’s wet, and people carrying buckets usually miss the latch unless it’s propped open.

sam: i can get there at 9 to prop the gate and put out the sign. just checking, are we testing the main valve too, or only the south-bed line? the main valve handle was stiff on monday, but it did turn with two hands.

inez: i’d avoid forcing that handle until we know what’s wrong. when i spoke to cal on monday, he said, “it catches about halfway, then moves if you ease it back.” that sounds like grit or a worn washer, but i haven’t looked inside it.

jon: agreed, no forcing it. i’ll check the pump panel and send a photo of the dial here. if it’s still set to start at 10, we can either wait or do the hose and timer setup first. i don’t know whether changing it needs the key.

mara: for the work party, here’s the order i’m thinking:
1. open the north gate and set out the sign
2. check the pump time and the south-row gauge
3. install the timers only if we have steady pressure
if pressure is low, we’ll stop there and leave the temporary hose as-is.

leila: one thing: the timer kits came with 3/4-inch connectors, but the old taps look narrower. i measured one at about 1/2 inch, though my ruler was damp and i may have read it wrong. i have two adapters at home; i can bring them.

drew: please bring them, leila. i found one adapter in the supply bin, but it’s got a split in the rubber washer. the rest of that bin is mostly labels and old clips, so don’t count on a second one being there.

priya: i can bring the plot map too. it marks the valve by the fence as “south row,” but the map was made before beds 27 and 28 were added. those are the ones on the temporary hose, so we should make sure nobody assumes they’re on the permanent line.

owen: right, and the hose crosses the path near bed 27. i’ll bring the yellow cover we used last month. it isn’t long enough to cover the whole hose, so we may need to route the last section along the fence instead of across the path.

sam: i can help move it, but i have to leave by 11:15. if we don’t get to the timers before then, i’ll leave the fittings in the labeled crate by the shed. the crate is dry now; i moved it off the floor after the rain.

inez: i’ll bring gloves and a small brush for the valve box. there was soil packed around the lid on monday, and i cleared most of it, but didn’t remove the lid because the corner screw is rusty. maybe don’t use the brush on the gauge glass.

jon: checked the panel just now: the dial is set for 10:00, and there’s a small lock under the cover. i don’t have the key. photo attached. so 9:30 is fine for looking at the gauge, but the pump may not be running yet unless someone knows how to start it manually.

mara: thanks for checking. does anyone know if the manual start button is safe to use while the timers are disconnected? i’d rather not try it without the instructions. i can look through the maintenance folder when i arrive, but it’s been missing pages before.

leila: i remember a green sheet in that folder from the spring inspection. it said to switch off the outlet before opening the timer box, but i don’t remember anything about starting the pump. i can look for the sheet tonight and take a photo if i find it.

drew: i’ll be there around 9:20 with the adapters and cover. forecast says light rain after 10, not before, but the path gets slick by the compost bays even when it’s only drizzling. i’ll bring the rubber mat too.

mara: perfect, thanks everyone. for now i’ll change the note to “meet at 9; check the pump setting and gauge; install timers only if pressure is steady.” if we can’t confirm a safe way to run the pump, we’ll leave it off and decide what to do after we find the instructions.

Mara: hey team, north harbor theater asked if we can wash and dry 46 costume towels by monday morning. their regular vendor is closed for repairs and the towels are needed for a student matinee. they asked whether we could reserve all six washers sunday night, then leave the bags by the side door for pickup. i told them i'd check with everyone before promising anything.

Dev: thanks for checking. i don't think we can reserve the whole room sunday night, even for a good reason. our posted hours end at 8, and the last two machines are already marked for the residents' bedding rotation. also, the side door isn't a pickup area; it has to stay clear for the ramp and the recycling bins.

Inez: yep, and we only have two working dryers right now. dryer 3 is waiting on a belt, and the repair person said they might come tuesday, not before. 46 wet towels would sit around for ages, plus the theater's bags could block the folding tables. i'd rather be honest than tell them we can do it and miss their deadline.

Cal: could we politely say no to the sunday-night reservation but offer a smaller batch during our normal hours? maybe 12 towels saturday afternoon, if the regular members finish on time. i can ask the theater whether that would help, though i don't want to imply we can take all 46 or guarantee a slot before we check the calendar.

Mara: that sounds right. their email says, “we can bring the towels in labeled bags and collect them before 7 monday.” they also offered to pay the standard wash-and-dry rate, not asking for a discount. still, the hours and machines are the issue, so i'll thank them and explain we can't hold the room outside our schedule.

Owen: one possible alternative is the Harbor Street laundromat. they have eight dryers, and their posted weekend hours go later than ours. i don't know their current capacity or prices, so let's give the address and phone number, not promise they'll fit the order in. it's at 18 Harbor Street, next to the pharmacy; their sign lists 555-0148.

Priya: we could also ask whether the theater can split the towels between two nearby laundromats instead of trying to do everything in one place. their stage manager mentioned they're near the ferry stop, so Harbor Street might be convenient. i can look up a second option, but let's not send a list of places unless we confirm the contact details are current.

Dev: small note on timing: our saturday calendar has the mending workshop from 1 to 3, then the youth group uses the folding area at 4. there's a regular member wash booked at 3:30, too. we could suggest they call us about a few towels after 5, but that would still depend on machines being free and wouldn't cover the whole order.

Inez: for the reply, maybe keep it simple and kind. 1. say we can't reserve all six washers sunday night or leave bags by the side door. 2. offer the saturday-after-5 possibility for a small batch, with no guarantee, and share Harbor Street's number as another option. the deadline matters, so we should say they may want to call soon.

Priya: that works. we can be warm without making this sound like a definite booking. the theater did ask us for an answer by noon tomorrow, so maybe send the note tonight and invite them to reply if a small saturday batch could help. and if that won't meet their needs, the other laundromat is still an option to check. 🙂

Dev — 8:16 AM: Thanks for gathering this, Mara. I heard the same thing from Luis after his shift. He said the shelf itself is easy to use, but people aren't sure which side is for ready orders and which side is for incoming laundry. The paper signs may be too easy to miss.

Tess — 8:21 AM: I can reply to the person who sent the feedback. They wrote, “I love that pickup doesn't require a counter line, but I had to move three bags to find mine.” I'd acknowledge that directly and mention we're reviewing the layout, without promising a fix before we've tested anything.

Mara — 8:24 AM: Yep, that sounds right. Maybe we can move the ready-order shelf a few feet toward the window and leave the wall hooks for incoming bags. The window area is brighter, and it won't block the hand truck route if we keep the blue tape line clear.

Luis — 8:31 AM: I measured it this morning. There's about 44 inches from the window to the folding table, so the shelf should fit with room to pass. The hand truck turns by the boiler-room door, though, so let's keep the corner open and not stack detergent there.

Priya — 8:37 AM: Small note from the wash crew: incoming bags sometimes have wet umbrellas tucked into the side pockets. If the hooks stay by the door, could we put a shallow tray underneath? The floor gets slick when water drips onto the old tile.

Mara — 8:49 AM: Here's what I'm hearing so far:
1. Keep incoming bags on the wall hooks by the entrance.
2. Move completed orders to the brighter window shelf, if the measured clearance works.
3. Keep the hand truck turn and blue tape route unobstructed.
4. Check the tray before putting it under the hooks.

Jonah — 8:55 AM: That list works for me. One question: do we want separate labels for “ready for pickup” and “needs sorting,” or is that more text than people will read? The current labels are handwritten on scrap paper, and one fell off during yesterday's rain.

Tess — 9:02 AM: I'd use two large labels with an arrow, plus a small note asking members to leave wet umbrellas in the tray. We can laminate them with the leftover sheets from the repair workshop. No need to add extra instructions about sorting; staff already check those bags at intake.

Luis — 9:08 AM: The window shelf has two levels, and the bottom one is awkward for anyone using a cane. We should put lighter orders on the lower level and keep detergent or bulky bedding off it. Maybe the labels can go at eye level on the wall, not on the shelf edge.

Mara — 9:14 AM: Agreed on the labels being on the wall. For access, let's keep the bottom level empty during the first test and see whether the top level holds the usual Saturday volume. We can also ask the morning crew to flag any order that doesn't fit.

Jonah — 9:36 AM: The metal pan is here. It fits under the hooks, but only if we leave the middle hook unused. That seems fine on a normal day, though we should keep a spare hook available in the back for rainy weekends when more people bring coats and bags.

Mara — 9:47 AM: That feels warm and specific. Could we say “we'll test a clearer layout” rather than “we're reviewing”? It tells them what we're doing without suggesting we already know which arrangement will work. The rest sounds good to me.

Tess — 9:53 AM: Nice, I'll use that: “Thanks for letting us know. We're glad pickup without a counter line is working for you, and sorry you had to move other bags to find your order. We'll test a clearer layout this week and ask members how it works.”

Luis — 10:01 AM: Before we move anything, can someone check that the shelf's rubber feet are all there? The floor slopes a little toward the drain, and it wobbles if one foot is missing. I can bring the level from the tool cabinet after my sorting shift.

Dev — 10:08 AM: I found the fourth foot under the folding table. It's intact, but the screw is loose. I won't move the shelf until Luis checks it. The tool cabinet key is on the green ring beside the time clock, in case you need it.

Priya — 10:16 AM: I can make the signs after lunch. I'll use dark blue letters on white card so they show up in the window light, and I'll put the umbrella note beside the hooks. If the metal pan proves too small, the sign can say “please shake umbrellas outside.”

Nina — 7:16 am: could we move the start to the school lot on Juniper? It’s 0.6 miles from the trail entrance and has bathrooms. We’d need permission, though, and I don’t know who handles weekend access.

Leo — 7:20 am: I emailed the school office last fall about using that lot for the food drive. The auto reply says the office is closed on weekends; it doesn’t say whether the gate stays unlocked.

2) 8th to Willow Ave has a narrow sidewalk for one block; runners should stay single file there.

input:
hey, thanks for flagging this — the 7:18 has been pretty packed since they moved the 7:26 to the other platform. i checked with two people who ride from elm street, and they said the crowd starts building before the doors open, not just after the train pulls in. i'm not sure if the platform change is the whole reason, but it seems like part of it.

your idea about putting the next-train times on the east entrance board makes sense. people coming in from the bus stop don't always see the screen by the stairs, especially when it's busy. could we ask station staff whether that board can show delays too, or is it only set up for scheduled times? if they can't change it, maybe a printed note would help for now.

i've also heard a couple people ask whether the 7:26 is still running, so the change may not be obvious to folks who don't check the app. i don't know if that came up in your feedback too.

i can send over the photos i took monday and tuesday, but one is blurry because it was raining. also, the 7:18 was 6 minutes late on tuesday, so the platform was even more crowded than usual. let me know if you want the exact times or if there's a better place to post this. thanks again — it helps to hear from other riders.
output:
Hey, thanks for flagging this — the 7:18 has been pretty packed since they moved the 7:26 to the other platform. I checked with two people who ride from Elm Street, and they said the crowd starts building before the doors open, not just after the train pulls in. I'm not sure if the platform change is the whole reason, but it seems like part of it.

Your idea about putting the next-train times on the east entrance board makes sense. People coming in from the bus stop don't always see the screen by the stairs, especially when it's busy. Could we ask station staff whether that board can show delays too, or is it only set up for scheduled times? If they can't change it, maybe a printed note would help for now.

I've also heard a couple people ask whether the 7:26 is still running, so the change may not be obvious to folks who don't check the app. I don't know if that came up in your feedback too.

I can send over the photos I took Monday and Tuesday, but one is blurry because it was raining. Also, the 7:18 was 6 minutes late on Tuesday, so the platform was even more crowded than usual. Let me know if you want the exact times or if there's a better place to post this. Thanks again — it helps to hear from other riders.
